# How AI Works for Kids

> Free, ad-free games that show kids ages 6–14 how AI works. No accounts, no ads, and no live chatbot. Built by Nick Castro in Chicago.

This site teaches with local mini-games. It does not open a chat with an AI model. Kid-facing titles avoid jargon. Tweens can see a small grown-up name on each lesson (patterns, training, context, correlation, attention, RAG, AI safety).

## Pages

- [Home](https://howaiworksforkids.com/): What the site is and the lesson path
- [Lessons](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons): All seven games
- [For parents and teachers](https://howaiworksforkids.com/parents): How to use the lessons. Lessons stay free; no checkout or teacher login
- [About Nick Castro](https://howaiworksforkids.com/about): Portfolio context and links
- [Tested by real kids](https://howaiworksforkids.com/tested-by-kids): Placeholder only. No invented quotes
- [Privacy](https://howaiworksforkids.com/privacy): COPPA-friendly notice

## Lessons

- [AI isn't magic](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/not-magic): It finds patterns
- [Learn by trying](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/learn-by-trying): Practice and feedback
- [Words need context](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/words-need-context): The same word can change meaning
- [Tricky look-alikes](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/tricky-look-alikes): False patterns and correlation traps
- [What it pays attention to](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/what-it-notices): The question picks the clue
- [Check a source](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/check-a-source): Look it up before answering
- [Be safe and honest](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/be-safe-and-honest): AI can be wrong, privacy, ask a grown-up
